title: Smooth schemes over fields are geometrically normal
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a scheme with a smooth morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then $X$ is geometrically regular, geometrically normal, and geometrically reduced over $k$: for every finite purely inseparable field extension $K'/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], the base change $X_{K'}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K'$ [def-pc-base-change] is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]; for every field extension $K/k$, every local ring of $X_K$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] and $X_K$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme].

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary field extension $K/k$ and put $Y=X_K$ with structure map $f_K:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. Clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change] applies to the smooth map $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the field-extension map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, so $f_K$ is smooth. This requires neither a fixed relative dimension nor quasi-compactness of $X$.

source.place: Tag 01VB, lemma-base-change-smooth; applied as in varieties.tex, Tag 056T

proof.text: By [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $f_K$ is locally of finite presentation. Its affine neighbourhoods in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] can have target $\operatorname{Spec}K$, since this field spectrum has only one nonempty open. They give an affine open cover $Y=\bigcup_i U_i$ with $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ and $B_i\cong K[t_1,\ldots,t_{n_i}]/(g_1,\ldots,g_{m_i})$. The images of the $t_j$ generate $B_i$ as a $K$-algebra. Thus $f_K$ is locally of finite type, and each $U_i\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is of finite type: its single affine chart is a finite affine covering as required in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 01TP, definition-finite-presentation; Tag 01T1, definition-finite-type; the local-finite-type input of varieties.tex, Tag 056S, lemma-smooth-regular

proof.text: Every ideal of the field $K$ is either zero or the unit ideal, so $K$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Its one-point spectrum is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact, hence Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] separately to each finite-type map $U_i\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ from Step 2. Each $U_i$ is Noetherian. Its affine open neighbourhoods with Noetherian coordinate rings, furnished by local Noetherianity, are also affine open neighbourhoods in $Y$. They cover $Y$, so [pqf-def-locnoeth] makes $Y$ locally Noetherian. No finite cover of all of $Y$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian, applied to the finite-type affine charts; Properties Tag 01OV, definition-noetherian

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-regularity-smooth-field-criterion] over the field $K$ to $f_K$, smooth by Step 1 and locally of finite type by Step 2. Take its finitely generated extension $L/K$ to be the identity extension $K/K$. The identity base change $Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}K\cong Y$ is given by the projection, with inverse $(\operatorname{id}_Y,f_K)$, by [def-pc-base-change]. The criterion therefore says that every local ring of $Y$ is regular. Together with Step 3, the equivalence in [def-weil-regular-scheme] says that $Y$ is regular. This holds for every $K/k$, in particular for every finite purely inseparable $K'/k$, as required for the geometrically regular clause.

source.place: Tag 038X, lemma-geometrically-regular-smooth; Tag 056S, lemma-smooth-regular; Properties Tag 02IT, lemma-characterize-regular; Tag 056T, regularity conclusion

proof.text: For the same arbitrary field extension $K/k$, apply clause (1) of [rem-pc-regular-normal] to the regular scheme $Y$ of Step 4. It gives that $Y$ is normal, which that node defines explicitly as every local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ being an integral domain integrally closed in its field of fractions. This is exactly the normal-domain conclusion for every local ring of $X_K$; since $K/k$ was arbitrary, $X$ is geometrically normal.

source.place: Tag 0569, lemma-regular-normal; this is the last cited lemma of the proof of varieties.tex, Tag 056T

proof.text: For every field extension $K/k$, Step 5 makes each local ring of $X_K$ a domain. In a domain, $a^n=0$ with $n\geq1$ implies $a=0$, by induction on $n$ using the absence of zero divisors. Hence all these local rings are reduced, so $X_K$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. This proves the geometrically reduced clause, including when $X_K$ is empty, where there are no stalks to check.

source.place: Tag 056T, reducedness conclusion; Schemes Tag 01J0, definition-reduced
